transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-04-18 11:00 PT | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jared O'Neill (Redwood SE), Ivy Park (Redwood Solutions Eng); Priya Rao (CTO, GammaWorks), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Sofia Mendes (Security Lead), Tom Alvarez (ML Eng)

Summary: quick intro, goals, technical constraints, deep dive into integration patterns, agree pilot next steps.

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, i'll kick off, we can do a quick intros, and then jared will dive into tech.
00:16 Priya Rao: hi thanks, priya here, CTO at gammaworks; we're evaluating options to run our inference layer — want to understand hosted vs dedicated vs private and how it ties into our gateway.
00:32 Liam O'Connor: quick context, we run a multi-tenant platform, primary requirements are latency under 250ms p95 for short chat flows, and strict tenant isolation for some customers. also, we use envoy as our api gateway.
00:47 Jared O'Neill: great, thanks. quick question, do you currently use any LLM orchestration libs like langchain or llamaindex in prod?
00:54 Tom Alvarez: we have some experiments with langchain for chains, and llm-index for retrieval augmented flows, mostly in staging; production is a bit custom.
01:08 Ivy Park: ok good to know. objective for today: map integration points — sdk usage, gateway/proxy pattern, rate limits/quotas mapping, and observability hooks — so we can scope a pilot.
01:22 Priya Rao: yes, and also security — saml sso, audit logs, kms, and data residency for eu customers.
01:30 Maya Chen: totally. quick high level: redwood offers hosted api (fastest), dedicated pools (reserved gpus & tenancy), and private (vpc or on-prem). same api surface across all. we'll talk tradeoffs.

02:05 Jared O'Neill: tech deep dive — first integration topology. Option A: direct hosted calls from your backend to redwood api via a proxy (envoy) — simplest; Option B: a gateway sidecar that handles caching, batching, and per-tenant routing; Option C: private deployment inside your vpc or on-prem for strict isolation. pros/cons?
02:30 Liam O'Connor: can you clarify difference between proxy and sidecar for us?
02:34 Jared O'Neill: sure. proxy (envoy) is external routing — you put rate-limits and per-tenant headers there. sidecar sits next to each service and can do local batching, KV caching (we sometimes say KV "cash" in transcrip), and shorter hop latencies. sidecar more work but lowers cross-service traffic.
02:50 Sofia Mendes: for PCI-like customers we probably need private; for others dedicated sounds sufficient. question about key management — if we go private, can we bring our own KMS/HSM?
03:05 Maya Chen: yes, private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; we also provide audit logs and forwardable immutable traces. for dedicated we offer KMS integrations via cloud provider keys.

03:35 Tom Alvarez: integration with langchain — do you have an official adapter?
03:41 Jared O'Neill: we have a maintained langchain adapter snippet; i'll share a repo. it includes streaming, function calling shim, and an example with llms + retrievers. for llamaindex we have a connector pattern sample — not a first-class pkge but extensible.
03:59 Ivy Park: note, those are in our examples repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/langchain-adapter and a short demo notebook.
04:12 Priya Rao: perfect. on rate limits — we need per-tenant quotas with burst control and throttling back to failover model; how granular can redwood be?
04:24 Jared O'Neill: we support token-based quotas and per-route limits. you can map to tenant id in headers, or use api keys per-tenant. burst windows are configurable; can set soft quotas (warn) and hard quotas (reject).
04:38 Liam O'Connor: does the gateway enforce token accounting or does redwood return cost per request?
04:43 Jared O'Neill: redwood returns token cost metadata and per-token billing. you can also enable token-level tracing for observability plug-ins, and our console shows token breakdown per request id. we also emit traces compatible with datadog/jaeger.

05:10 Sofia Mendes: logging & audit — do you write full request/response bodies to logs by default? data retention?
05:18 Maya Chen: by default we do not persist sensitive inputs for hosted; you can opt-in for debug. for private/dedicated we can configure retention policies and support immutable audit logs forwarded to your SIEM. we integrate with S3 and GCS sinks.
05:34 Priya Rao: what about redaction at ingestion? can you redact pii client-side, or does redwood provide redaction?
05:40 Jared O'Neill: we support client-side preprocessing and also server-side filtering where you can supply regex rules; but best practice is to pre-redact before sending.

06:05 Tom Alvarez: benchmark question — we want to test 8k context model with typical chat loads (50rps burst to 200rps) and p95 under 250ms for short sequences; is that realistic on dedicated?
06:20 Jared O'Neill: for short sequences (<128 tokens) dedicated pools sized properly and with batching disabled or small batch windows can meet 200-250ms p95; we'll run a pilot with your sample traffic to tune batching and kernel selection.
06:35 Liam O'Connor: on batching — can we control batching window or disable continuous batching?
06:39 Jared O'Neill: yes, there are batching knobs per-route; you can set max latency, max batch size, or even use a sync mode for deterministic latency. continuous batching is on by default for cost efficiency.

07:05 Priya Rao: observability — what traces do you emit? we need request->model->tokens span and ability to link to our trace id.
07:14 Ivy Park: we emit open-telemetry spans for request lifecycle, model invoke spans, and tokenization spans. you can pass in a traceparent header and we'll propagate it. console shows route level latency, token counts, and cost.
07:30 Sofia Mendes: can we ingest those spans into our jaeger instance?
07:34 Ivy Park: yes, we support exporting to your OTLP collector or pulling via our export connectors.

08:00 Priya Rao: security review — SSO and RBAC. we need SAML SSO and ability to map roles to console actions.
08:10 Maya Chen: we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC with granular permissions for model deploy, viewing billing, and audit read. we can add IP allowlists for admin console.
08:24 Sofia Mendes: for compliance, we need proof of SOC2 plus pen-test report.
08:29 Maya Chen: we'll share SOC2 report and a redacted pen-test summary in the security pack after the call.

08:55 Tom Alvarez: about retriever workflows — we use an internal vector DB and llm-index. how do you recommend connecting?
09:02 Jared O'Neill: two patterns: keep vector store inside your infra and call redwood for generation (we stream context only), or push top-k docs as context via our embeddings + prompt chunking; we have examples for both. if privacy is a must, private deployment keeps vector store inside your VPC.
09:21 Liam O'Connor: if we do sidecar, can it do KV caching of model KV cache to speed up multi-turn dialogs?
09:27 Jared O'Neill: sidecar can manage KV caching for recurrent sessions; we also provide prefix/KV caching in our runtime for common flows. note that cross-tenant cache isolation is enforced.

10:00 Priya Rao: latency vs cost — some stakeholders want lowest cost (batching + quantization) others want predictable low latency. what's recomendation?
10:12 Ivy Park: for predictable low latency go dedicated with tuned batch knobs and smaller quantized model variants; for lowest cost use hosted with more aggressive batching and quantized model variants. we can recommend quantization profile per workload during pilot.
10:29 Priya Rao: how disruptive is switching from hosted to private later?
10:34 Maya Chen: we expose the same api and client sdk; switching routes is mostly config and routing changes. you may need to re-provision keys and update networking, but app code remains the same.

11:00 Tom Alvarez: question: does redwood support function-calling and structured output? we leverage that heavily.
11:07 Jared O'Neill: yes, streaming + function calling + structured output is supported across modes. for private, ensure your runtime has the right model kernels, but interface is same.

12:10 Priya Rao: regulatory question — do you support EU data residency?
12:16 Maya Chen: yes hosted regions in eu, dedicated can be region-restricted, private full control. we can produce DPA with residency clauses.

12:50 Sofia Mendes: on audit logs, we need retention of 7 years for certain customers; is that possible?
12:56 Maya Chen: for private deployments yes; for hosted we offer configurable retention windows up to X (we'll add the exact number in the docs). we'll include retention SLAs in the security pack.

13:30 Liam O'Connor: rate limiting enforcement — can it be done at the gateway with shadow mode before flipping to enforcement?
13:37 Jared O'Neill: yes, deploy with shadow mode to surface expected rejects, then flip to hard enforcement. we provide metrics and sampler traces to validate.

14:05 Tom Alvarez: about the SDK, we need a tiny JS/Go adapter to integrate with our gateway so we can add tenant headers and do pre-flight checks.
14:16 Ivy Park: we have official SDKs in JS, Python, and Go. the JS sdk has middleware hooks to inject tenant id and to collect token metrics. we'll send sample go middleware.

15:00 Priya Rao: can you do a bench with our sample dataset? we'll provide synthetic users.
15:06 Jared O'Neill: yes, pilot plan: 2-week onramp with a small dedicated pool or private trial. step 1: share prompts and traffic patterns, step 2: redwood runs bench, step 3: adjust batching/quantization and re-run.

16:00 Maya Chen: any blockers we haven't covered?
16:05 Sofia Mendes: one on legal — do you support per-tenant encryption keys for data at rest?
16:12 Maya Chen: yes with private we can integrate customer-managed keys; dedicated via cloud kms with per-tenant encryption by design.

17:20 Priya Rao: timeline — we want pilot started within 2 weeks and decision by quarter end.
17:27 Maya Chen: that aligns; we'll aim to share security pack within 48 hours and schedule pilot by monday.

17:50 Jared O'Neill: quick note on observability hooks: our telemetry exporter supports OTLP, and we also provide a webhook to push cost events per request. you can ingest into your billing pipeline to back-charge tenants.
18:12 Liam O'Connor: that webhook is critical, we need per-request token cost to show usage in our dashboard.
18:19 Ivy Park: yep we'll attach sample event schemas and a connector.

18:45 Tom Alvarez: small nit — when streaming tokens do you guarantee ordering and reconnect behavior?
18:50 Jared O'Neill: we guarantee ordered streaming; reconnect semantics are documented — resumable via request id for short windows. we'll share the exact behavior and sample code.

19:25 Priya Rao: what about model rollouts and A/B testing? we need canaries and automated fallback if perf regresses.
19:32 Maya Chen: rollouts: canary + automatic fallback policies by latency or quality metrics; you can configure A/B and collect evals back into our optimize module.
19:45 Sofia Mendes: any mention of data used for model training? we need non-retention guarantee.
19:50 Maya Chen: by default we do not use customer payloads for training; there is an opt-in program for synthetic improvement but enterprise customers can opt out. we'll include the clause in DPA.

20:25 Jared O'Neill: i'll summarize tech next steps: share langchain + llm-index adapter repos, sample go middleware, bench plan template, and an initial config file for sidecar vs proxy setups.
20:38 Maya Chen: i'll follow-up on security pack and commercial terms; ivy will help with onboarding playbook.

21:00 Priya Rao: perfect. specific ask: include a sample rate-limit policy mapping for per-tenant quotas and an example of how to surface rejects to end users.
21:12 Jared O'Neill: noted. we'll include a policy template and a sample error payload.

21:30 Tom Alvarez: one more on proxies — do you have recommendations tying into envoy-rate-limit filter or should we use redwood routing?
21:38 Jared O'Neill: envoy filter is common; you can enforce locally and then let redwood be the source-of-truth for billing/backup enforcement. we provide a small envoy plugin example.

22:05 Maya Chen: ok let's do a recap and next steps.
22:10 Maya Chen: recap: redwood to send security pack (SOC2, KMS/HSM docs, pen-test summary), SE to share langchain/llamaindex examples and go middleware, redwood + gammaworks to run 2-week bench/pilot with sample dataset, and schedule pilot kickoff.
22:30 Priya Rao: agreed. thanks everyone, looking forward to the pilot.
22:36 Sofia Mendes: thanks, we'll send compliance checklist by friday.
22:40 Maya Chen: great, i'll circulate notes and timeline after the call. thanks all.

End of transcript.
